author: desk
note: Desk-written plain-English summary, not a tiered fact. Written to help a reader understand the business quickly; verify any figure against the fact store before using it in a report.
one_liner: Elon Musk's AI company, now held within SpaceX.
what_it_does: xAI builds the Grok family of AI models and integrates them into X, the social network. Its distinguishing asset is real-time access to posts on X as training and retrieval material. Following a corporate reorganisation it sits inside SpaceX rather than standing alone, which changes how any stake in it should be valued.
how_it_makes_money: Subscriptions bundled into X's paid tiers, a developer interface, and enterprise arrangements. Revenue is small relative to its valuation and disclosure is thin.
why_it_matters: It is the clearest case in the group where corporate structure, rather than product, determines what an investor actually owns.
competitive_position: Competes at the frontier on model quality while trailing on enterprise adoption. Its compute build-out has been unusually fast.
key_risks: Being held inside SpaceX means an investor's exposure is indirect and hard to value separately.
Disclosure is the thinnest of any company in this coverage.
Heavy dependence on one founder whose attention is split across several companies.
Revenue is far behind the valuation implied by recent rounds.

glossary.definition: Which legal entity actually owns the business. It determines what a shareholder owns and how easily it can be sold.
